expectations.text: rule.yaml has queryPeriod strictly longer than queryFrequency (no zero-overlap 1h/1h window) or the query selects the run window on ingestion_time()
expectations.evidence: queryFrequency: 1h (line 18), queryPeriod: 2h (line 19); 2h > 1h. Additionally the run window is selected on ingestion time: line 75 '| where coalesce(ingestion_time(), TimeGenerated) > now() - query_frequency'.

expectations.text: The query handles ingestion delay explicitly: it uses ingestion_time() or declares a delay/wait window (e.g. let query_wait / ingestion_delay) that is added to the scan window
expectations.evidence: Line 36 'let ingestion_delay = 1h;' with lines 34-35 documenting 'Scan window on event time = query_frequency + ingestion_delay' (query_period = 2h). Line 74 '| where TimeGenerated >= now() - query_period' is the wide event-time scan and line 75 '| where coalesce(ingestion_time(), TimeGenerated) > now() - query_frequency' is the exact run slice - this is the documented Microsoft pattern (wider TimeGenerated scan + ingestion_time() > ago(frequency)). Note query_period is a literal 2h, not computed from query_frequency + ingestion_delay, but the comment makes the relationship explicit.

claims.evidence: python3 yaml.safe_load succeeded; 21 top-level keys including id, kind: Scheduled. No 'status' field (optional in the repo format but present in most current templates).

claims.claim: KQL is plausibly valid for Log Analytics
claims.evidence: Parentheses 49/49 and brackets 4/4 balanced in non-comment code. SigninLogs columns referenced (TimeGenerated, IPAddress, UserPrincipalName, ResultType, AppDisplayName, ClientAppUsed, UserAgent, Location, AutonomousSystemNumber) are real. materialize(), 'between (1 .. n)', 'in ((Candidates | project IPAddress))', join kind=inner ... on IPAddress followed by project-away IPAddress1, take_any, strcat with numeric args, coalesce(ingestion_time(), TimeGenerated) are all valid constructs. No syntax errors spotted.

claims.claim: Every customDetails / alertDetailsOverride column survives the final projection
claims.evidence: SprayedAccounts, TotalFailures, TotalSuccesses, CredentialValidatedCount, CredentialValidatedAccounts, SampleAccounts, DetectionReason, Severity and IPAddress all exist after the join/extends and project-reorder removes nothing; dynamic set columns are tostring()'d at lines 124-125.

Schedule, ingestion window and thresholds are all declared once at the top with comments; ingestion_time() slicing prevents duplicate alerts across runs; IPv6 null-handling for ipv4_is_in_any_range is explicit (line 79). Minor: the description says 'at most 3 failures per sprayed account in the hourly run window' but per-account failure counts are taken over the 2h TimeGenerated scan, so an account can accumulate failures from the previous run's slice too; query_period is a literal rather than query_frequency + ingestion_delay.

suggestions.assertion: The query handles ingestion delay explicitly: it uses ingestion_time() or declares a delay/wait window (e.g. let query_wait / ingestion_delay) that is added to the scan window
suggestions.reason: The assertion accepts a declared delay variable regardless of how it is used. A 'let ingestion_delay' that is only referenced in a post-aggregation recency guard (run A) and one that actually bounds the run slice via ingestion_time() (run B) both pass, yet only the latter prevents hourly re-alerting on the same events. Consider requiring that the run window itself is selected on ingestion_time().

suggestions.assertion: rule.yaml includes incident grouping or suppression settings (incidentConfiguration.groupingConfiguration or suppressionDuration) or alert enrichment (customDetails / alertDetailsOverride)
suggestions.reason: Trivially satisfiable: any rule with a customDetails block passes even with no incident grouping or suppression. All three runs pass; the OR makes it non-discriminating. Split into 'incident grouping configured' and 'customDetails/alertDetailsOverride columns exist in the output'.

No assertion checks that customDetails / alertDetailsOverride placeholder columns actually survive the final projection (only the IP entity column is checked). This was correct in all three runs but is a common deploy-time failure and worth its own assertion.

No assertion checks for the time-window coupling trap: a hard-coded 'where TimeGenerated > ago(X)' inside the query that must equal queryPeriod (run A) silently diverges from the YAML when either is edited. 'Deploy without surprises' arguably covers this.

eval_feedback.overall: This run satisfies every assertion with substantive evidence; the only non-discriminating assertion is 8 (OR of three independent features).
